body.statement: Can one prove comparison and uniqueness for bounded semicontinuous viscosity sub- and supersolutions of \(\mathcal G_\lambda F=0\) on \(\mathcal D\), with the generalized terminal traces selected by the fixed closed-test payoff, at every viable off-origin state including \(Q_j(t)=0\) faces and threshold-equality states?
body.justification: A statewise uniqueness theorem would turn the initial-value envelope selection into a complete generalized-terminal HJB theory.
body.gap: Adusumilli's comparison theorem covers Hölder data; the initial-state modulus here does not identify every off-origin boundary trace.
body.consumer: A positive answer would justify reusable feedback values after arbitrary interim states, rather than only design-time evaluation from the origin.

obligation.what_is_open: Comparison and uniqueness at every viable off-origin state remain unproved.
obligation.obstruction: The common-drift translation changes only future information from an off-origin state. A coordinate frozen after that state receives no strict terminal displacement, so the origin argument does not order the two generalized terminal traces there.
obligation.attempted: I propagated the shift coupling on the remaining time interval and checked zero-allocation faces. This reproduces the initial-state squeeze only when every near-critical intersection contains a coordinate receiving enough future clock; that property fails on general viable faces and cannot be imposed without changing the control class.
obligation.partial_result:
Starting from a viable state \((t_0,x,q)\), the same common-drift coupling
changes only future scores:
\[
X_j(s)\longmapsto X_j(s)+e\{Q_j(s)-q_j\},
\qquad t_0\leq s\leq1,
\]
and its relative-entropy cost is
\[
\frac{e^2}{2}\sum_j\{Q_j(1)-q_j\}
=\frac{e^2}{2}(1-t_0).
\]
Thus the initial-state comparison proof extends statewise whenever every
intersection within \(\delta\) of threshold contains a coordinate whose
remaining allocation is at least a declared positive amount.  At the
origin this follows without forced exploration because an unsampled
coordinate has \(X_j=Q_j=0\) and elementary e-value one.  At a general
off-origin state, however, a near-critical intersection can be supported
entirely on coordinates receiving zero future clock.  Its terminal value is
then unchanged by every such translation.  The quantitative initial-state
squeeze is therefore proved, but it supplies neither an ordering of the two
generalized terminal traces nor comparison on all of \(\mathcal D\).
